venues.name: Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve

venues.name: Bvlgari Resort Bali

credentials: Tatler Indonesia, Hotel of the Year 2026

venues.name: Amankila
venues.note: Aman's three-tiered pools cascade to a private black-sand cove, the quiet east, far from the crowds.

venues.name: Amandari
venues.note: A hilltop Balinese village above the Ayung gorge, Aman's original Bali house, still peerless.

venues.name: Capella Ubud
venues.note: Bill Bensley's tented camp in the rainforest, theatre, craft and jungle in equal measure.
credentials: Travel + Leisure, Best Upcountry Hotels in Indonesia 2026

venues.name: Raffles Bali
venues.note: A hillside of just 32 pool villas above Jimbaran Bay, with Raffles butlers and a serious wellness spine.

Condé Nast Traveler, Top Destination Spa Resorts in the World

venues.name: Desa Potato Head

Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice 2024 & 2025, top hotel in Southeast Asia
Travel + Leisure, Best Beach Resorts in Indonesia 2026

credentials: Travel + Leisure, Best Upcountry Hotels in Indonesia 2026 (No. 4)

venues.name: COMO Uma Canggu

venues.name: COMO Uma Ubud
venues.note: A smaller, calmer COMO among the rice fields, Ubud wellness at a gentler scale.

LVMH Cheval Blanc / Belmond-adjacent maison pedigree

venues.name: Soori Bali

venues.name: Viceroy Bali

venues.name: The Oberoi Beach Resort, Bali
venues.note: The house that set the Bali standard, thatched garden villas and lawns running to Seminyak sand.
credentials: Oberoi, Leading Hotels of the World heritage; long-running Condé Nast / Travel + Leisure honours

venues.name: Nihi Bali (formerly Chapung Sebali)
venues.note: A cliff-edge Ubud retreat of villas above a jungle ravine, dramatic, design-forward, serene.

venues.name: Regent Bali Canggu
venues.note: Regent's return to Bali on the fashionable Canggu coast, polished, contemporary, of-the-moment.
credentials: Travel + Leisure, Best Beach Resorts in Indonesia 2026

venues.name: Nirjhara
venues.note: A jungle-and-waterfall hideaway near the coast, rice paddies one side, cascade the other.

venues.name: Samsara Ubud
venues.note: An all-villa boutique retreat with a strong wellness and privacy focus, deep in Ubud green.

venues.name: The Purist Villas & Spa
venues.note: A tiny antique-filled villa house among the rice fields, Ubud character without resort scale.

venues.name: Bisma Eight
venues.note: A design-forward small hotel walkable to central Ubud, with a canopy-level pool over the jungle.

venues.name: Chapung SeBali Resort & Spa
venues.note: Cliffside villas over the Ayung tributary with a much-photographed arch pool, great value for the drama.

venues.name: Lost Lindenberg
venues.note: Timber tree-house towers in a jungle by an untouristed black-sand beach, quietly radical, remote and calm.

venues.name: Blue Karma Village
venues.note: A cluster of private-pool villas in a quiet inland village, boutique value between the beaches.

venues.name: W Bali - Seminyak
venues.note: A high-energy design resort on Seminyak beach, pool scene, DJ nights and villas above the sand.
credentials: World Travel Awards, Indonesia's Leading Lifestyle Resort 2025
Travel + Leisure, Best Hotel Pools in Indonesia 2026

venues.name: Locavore NXT
venues.note: A forage-to-table 'localised rebellion', the most progressive kitchen in Indonesia, built on its own food system.

venues.name: Room4Dessert
venues.note: Will Goldfarb's dessert-led tasting theatre, the ex-elBulli mind who was named the world's best pastry chef.
credentials: The World's 50 Best Restaurants, World's Best Pastry Chef 2021 (Will Goldfarb)

venues.name: Kayuputi
venues.note: Pan-Asian haute cuisine on the Nusa Dua beachfront, with one of Bali's most decorated cellars.
credentials: Wine Spectator Best of Award of Excellence (16th consecutive year, 2025)

venues.name: Mozaic
venues.note: The restaurant that brought fine dining to Ubud, a quarter-century of French technique and Indonesian flavour.
credentials: Former World's 50 Best Restaurants listing (Chef Chris Salans)

venues.name: Merah Putih
venues.note: High-end Indonesian archipelago cooking under cathedral-like ceilings, arguably Bali's most beautiful room.

venues.name: Sangsaka
venues.note: A small, fire-driven kitchen doing one of the island's most exciting modern-Indonesian tasting menus.

venues.name: Sarong
venues.note: Chef Will Meyrick's street-food-to-fine-dining journey across Asia, glamorous and generous.
credentials: Recognised among Asia's best (Chef Will Meyrick)

venues.name: Mamasan
venues.note: Will Meyrick's other room, 1920s-Shanghai theatre and bold pan-Asian street flavours.

venues.name: Métis
venues.note: Grand French-Mediterranean dining over the rice fields, a long-standing Seminyak occasion address.

venues.name: Barbacoa
venues.note: Latin-American open-fire and wood-smoke cooking in a soaring warehouse, bold, generous, fun.

venues.name: Hujan Locale
venues.note: Will Meyrick's Ubud house for regional Indonesian home cooking, unfussy, warm, deeply of-the-island.

venues.name: Bambu
venues.note: Fine Indonesian dining in a lantern-lit garden pavilion, one of Seminyak's most atmospheric rooms.

venues.name: Api Jiwa
venues.note: An open-fire chef's-counter grilling over Indonesian binchotan and flame, smoke, char and craft.

venues.name: Kaum
venues.note: Heritage Indonesian recipes gathered from across the archipelago, cooking with a preservation mission.
credentials: Within Desa Potato Head, World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 18)

venues.name: Ijen at Desa Potato Head
venues.note: A zero-waste, fire-led tasting kitchen inside Bali's most awarded design hotel.
credentials: Within Desa Potato Head, World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 18)

venues.name: Mauri
venues.note: A refined Italian-leaning fine-dining newcomer that has climbed straight to the island's best-of lists.

venues.name: Night Rooster
venues.note: Locavore's cocktail bar, theatrical, botanical drinks built on Indonesian folklore and native ingredients.
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery (Night Rooster by Locavore NXT)

venues.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka
venues.note: Ubud's most famous suckling-pig warung, the honest, non-negotiable taste of Balinese food.

venues.name: Bridges Bali
venues.note: A river-gorge restaurant and wine cellar spanning the Campuhan bridges, a long-standing Ubud institution.

venues.name: Bella Cibo
venues.note: Considered Italian cooking on the Canggu coast, a quiet favourite that keeps its standards high.

venues.name: Tanah Lot, the floating sea temple
venues.note: A 16th-century shrine on a black-rock islet that appears to float at high tide, one of Indonesia's most photographed silhouettes at sunset. The clifftop terraces let elders watch the light change in comfort while younger travellers walk down to the tide pools; a private driver-plus-guide turns the crowd into a manageable golden hour.

venues.name: Besakih, the Mother Temple
venues.note: Bali's largest and holiest Hindu complex, 23 temples terraced up the flank of Mount Agung, in use for over a thousand years and unharmed by the 1963 eruption that stopped at its steps. For Hindu travellers this is the spiritual heart of the island; a licensed guide explains the pura hierarchy and keeps the temple touts at bay.

venues.name: Tirta Empul holy-spring purification (Melukat)
venues.note: A sacred water temple founded in 962 AD where Balinese Hindus queue at carved spouts for Melukat, a purification ritual to cleanse mind and spirit. It resonates powerfully for Indian travellers who know the idea of holy-water darshan; a private guide (now required for the ritual) arranges a quiet early slot and a sarong, so it feels devotional rather than touristic.

venues.name: Lempuyang Temple, the Gates of Heaven
venues.note: A hilltop temple where two split gates frame Mount Agung to perfection, the island's most famous photograph (the 'water reflection' is a mirror trick the on-site photographer performs under the lens). Come before sunrise, before cloud swallows the volcano; a driver who leaves Ubud at 4am beats both the heat and the two-hour queue.

venues.name: Jatiluwih rice terraces & the Subak system
venues.note: Over 600 hectares of emerald terraces sculpted by a thousand-year-old cooperative irrigation system rooted in the Tri Hita Karana philosophy of harmony between people, nature and the divine. Cooler, quieter and far grander than the roadside terraces near Ubud, a walking trail and a warung lunch make an unhurried half-day for a private group.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cultural Landscape of Bali Province: the Subak System as a Manifestation of the Tri Hita Karana Philosophy

venues.name: Tegallalang rice terraces & the jungle swings
venues.note: The classic stepped valley just 20 minutes north of Ubud, clean paths, coconut palms and the giant swings that arc out over the paddies, catnip for teenagers and grandparents with a camera alike. Go early (before 8am) with a driver so you get the low-angle light and the terraces largely to yourselves.

venues.name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
venues.note: A 12.5-hectare jungle reserve in the heart of Ubud with three moss-covered 14th-century temples and 1,200 long-tailed macaques the Balinese hold sacred. A hit with multi-generational groups, just leave sunglasses and loose bags in the car, as the monkeys are quick and cheeky.

venues.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk at dawn
venues.note: A gentle two-kilometre spine of grassy ridge above a green valley, the loveliest free thing to do in Ubud, best walked at 6am when it is cool, soft-lit and nearly empty. Easy enough for most of the family, and a coffee stop at the top rewards the effort before the day heats up.

venues.name: Ubud Royal Palace & evening Legong / Barong dance
venues.note: The 19th-century Puri Saren Agung, still home to Ubud's royal family, hosts nightly traditional dance in its courtyard, Legong, the Ramayana ballet, or the Barong's battle of good and evil, set to live gamelan. Free to wander by day; an evening performance under the carved gates is the most accessible window into Balinese court culture.

venues.name: Ubud Art Market
venues.note: Across the road from the palace, a warren of stalls for ikat sarongs, woven baskets, silver and carved wood, good fun to browse and haggle, with your guide steering you to the better-quality vendors upstairs. A relaxed hour for the family before or after the dance.

venues.name: ARMA, Agung Rai Museum of Art
venues.note: A serene garden museum founded by a Balinese collector, spanning classical Kamasan bark painting, the celebrated 1930s Batuan and Pita Maha works, and foreign masters who fell for the island. The calmest, best-curated art stop in Ubud, and its cultural workshops (painting, dance) are a genuine private-hosted experience for older children.

venues.name: Neka Art Museum
venues.note: Six pavilions telling the chronological story of Balinese painting and its collision with visiting Western artists, arguably the most historically grounded collection on the island. Air-conditioned, unhurried and easy to pair with a Campuhan walk on the same morning.

venues.name: Blanco Renaissance Museum
venues.note: The flamboyant clifftop house-studio of Filipino-Spanish painter Don Antonio Blanco, perched above the Campuhan gorge with gilded frames, ornate architecture and river views. A quick, characterful stop, half art, half theatre, that photographs beautifully.

venues.name: Mount Batur sunrise trek
venues.note: A 2am start and a torch-lit climb up an active volcano to watch dawn break over the caldera and Lake Batur, with a hot-spring soak to follow. Best for the fitter, adventurous members of the family; a private guide, hot tea at the summit and a slower pace make it far more civilised than the group tours.

venues.name: Kintamani caldera lunch with Mount Batur views
venues.note: For those who'd rather not climb at 2am, the ridge restaurants of Kintamani deliver the whole caldera, volcano, black lava fields and lake, over a leisurely lunch. Cool mountain air, a private driver and a table on the rim make an effortless half-day from Ubud.

venues.name: Ulun Danu Beratan, the lake temple
venues.note: A 17th-century temple dedicated to the water goddess Dewi Danu, its multi-tiered meru shrines appearing to float on misty Lake Beratan at 1,200 metres. The cool highland setting is a gentle, photogenic stop for all ages, and unmistakably the temple on the 50,000-rupiah note.

venues.name: Munduk waterfalls & the highland trails
venues.note: A cool, cloud-forest village of clove and coffee plantations laced with jungle waterfall walks, the un-touristy alternative to Bali's crowded cascades. A guided morning trek here, ending in a country lunch, suits families who want green calm over beach heat.

venues.name: Twin Lakes, Buyan & Tamblingan
venues.note: Two serene crater lakes inside an extinct volcano, once a single body of water, now separated by a jungle land-bridge you can trek between past mossy shrines. A traditional dugout canoe crossing on Tamblingan is a quiet, storybook experience away from the crowds.

venues.name: Sekumpul Waterfall
venues.note: Widely rated Bali's most spectacular falls, a fan of seven cascades over 80 metres tall, reached by a 400-step jungle descent and a river crossing. It rewards effort with drama; for a softer version, a guide can position you at the viewpoint without the full scramble.

venues.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
venues.note: A powerful 15-metre curtain of water just 20 minutes from Ubud, the easiest 'proper' waterfall to reach, with a stepped path and a swimmable pool at the base. Best before 8am for light and space; an easy add-on to a Ubud rice-terrace morning.

venues.name: Sidemen Valley & ikat weaving
venues.note: The Bali that Ubud used to be, hand-tended rice terraces cascading toward Mount Agung, birdsong instead of scooters, and family workshops still weaving endek and songket ikat the old way. The most restful base on the island for a private villa; walk the paddies at dawn, watch a loom in the afternoon.

venues.name: Celuk village silversmithing
venues.note: Bali's 'silver village', where families have hand-worked gold and silver for generations, chisel, punch and granulation done at the bench in front of you. Book a private smithing session to design and make your own piece, or commission investment jewellery direct from the maker.

venues.name: Balinese cooking class
venues.note: Start with a dawn market walk for lemongrass, galangal and torch ginger, then grind your own bumbu base and cook a full Balinese spread over a shared table. Ubud's classes are famously vegetarian-friendly, a warm, hands-on afternoon that travels home with the family.

venues.name: Nusa Lembongan, mantas, mangroves & Devil's Tear
venues.note: The gentler, easier Nusa island, snorkel with harmless four-metre manta rays at Manta Bay, drift the mangroves, and watch the Devil's Tear blowholes explode at sunset. Calmer roads and clearer water than Penida make it the family-friendly island day from Bali.

venues.name: Seminyak, beach, boutiques & sunset dining
venues.note: Bali's most polished stretch of coast, designer boutiques, spas and a long west-facing beach lined with sundowner tables and beach clubs. The easy, cosmopolitan counterpoint to the temples and terraces, and a good first or last base close to the airport.

venues.name: The Yoga Barn
venues.note: One of Southeast Asia's largest yoga and healing centres, daily classes in every style, sound baths, meditation and a vegan garden café, all in a jungle setting. A discreet, drop-in way to fold wellness into an Ubud stay without committing to a full retreat.

venues.name: Ayung River white-water rafting
venues.note: A scenic Class II–III float down the Ayung through jungle gorge, past carved rock walls and hidden waterfalls, thrilling enough for teenagers, gentle enough for confident parents. The most family-friendly adrenaline on the island, run by well-established operators.

venues.name: Goa Gajah, the Elephant Cave
venues.note: A 9th–11th-century sanctuary with a menacing carved cave mouth, ancient bathing pools and both Hindu and Buddhist relics in the same grove. A quick, atmospheric archaeological stop that pairs naturally with Tirta Empul on a temple-focused morning.

venues.name: Tukad Cepung, the cave waterfall
venues.note: A slot-canyon cascade where midday light beams through the rock onto falling water, deep in a hidden gorge, one of Bali's most surreal photographs. A short, wet walk through the canyon makes it a fun mini-adventure for older children.

venues.name: Batur natural hot springs
venues.note: Mineral pools fed by volcanic springs on the shore of Lake Batur, looking straight up at the caldera, the traditional reward after a sunrise climb, but worth it on its own. A warm, restorative soak in the cool mountains, easy for every generation.

venues.name: Gili Islands day escape
venues.note: Three car-free, scooter-free specks of powder-white sand off Lombok, ringed by coral and green turtles, you get around by bicycle or horse-drawn cidomo. A fast boat from Bali delivers a day of snorkelling at Turtle Point and Coral Garden; Gili Meno and Gili Air are the serenest for families.

venues.name: Potato Head Beach Club
venues.note: The amphitheatre of shutters facing the sunset, the beach club that set the island's standard, and cleaned up its act too.
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars, Sustainable Bar Award (2018)

venues.name: 40 Thieves
venues.note: A hidden speakeasy above a ramen counter, tight, skilled cocktails and a room that tends to end up dancing.
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025, No. 99 (51–100 extended list)

venues.name: Night Rooster
venues.note: Locavore's planter's-club bar, where Bali's 'king of cocktails' builds drinks on fermented island fruit and homemade bitters.
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery (Night Rooster by Locavore NXT)
